newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel on alert for Moslem prayers.
newsitem.headline: Israel on alert for Moslem prayers.

text.p: Israel deployed extra paramilitary police in Jerusalem after the Islamic fundamentalist Hamas movement called for "total confrontations" with Israeli forces and settlers after Moslem Friday prayers.
About 3,000 police took up positions around the al-Aqsa mosque complex where they shot dead three Palestinian stone-throwers after prayers last Friday.
Security sources said police reinforcements were also sent to the outskirts of the West Bank town of Qalqilya, which is under PLO rule.
Israel has ringed towns with tanks and prevented Palestinians from travelling in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Since last week gunbattles and clashes have claimed the lives of 58 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers. The violence was triggered by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel beside the al-Aqsa complex, a site holy to Moslems and Jews.
Palestinians described the situation as tense but no serious clashes were reported.
Hamas has been weakened since Palestinian President Yasser Arafat cracked down on the group in March under pressure from Israel after a wave of suicide bombings.
But Israeli security sources said they took its call for fresh protests seriously.

"Hamas Movement calls our heroic people to come out after Friday prayers tomorrow in marches and total confrontations against the forces of the Zionist occupation and its herds of settlers," Hamas said on Thursday.

"The popular and military Palestinian resistance must remain the spearhead in confronting the Zionist designs and projects, until victory and liberation," added the statement, faxed to an international news agency in Beirut.
In the flashpoint West Bank town of Hebron, plainclothes Palestinian police mingled with crowds urging calm when Israel briefly lifted a curfew to allow shopping, witnesses said.

The Palestinian police have not yet deployed in Hebron, the last major Palestinian town still under occupation. But witnesses said members of the force, some with pistols and two-way radios, were trying with Israel's knowledge and approval to prevent youths from confronting the Israeli army.
